E1: GitHub, Application card: GitHub Copilot inline suggestions.
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/d0c59c59fadf92c3a44676a3ed7ed38a015379ca/content/copilot/responsible-use/inline-suggestions.md
Section 1, exact excerpt: "GitHub Copilot inline suggestions provide autocomplete-style suggestions as you work. These suggestions appear inline in your editor or in text fields on GitHub.com, helping you write code and pull request descriptions more quickly."
Section 4, exact excerpt: "Copilot can suggest test cases based on the surrounding code, including possible input parameters, expected output values, and assertions. This helps developers create test coverage more quickly, including edge cases and boundary conditions that might be difficult to identify manually. Generated tests should still be reviewed, as they may not cover all scenarios."
Section 6, exact excerpt: "The surrounding code from your cursor position is pre-processed by the inline suggestions system, combined with contextual information (such as code snippets from open tabs in the editor), and sent to a large language model in the form of a prompt."
Section 7, exact excerpt: "Copilot may generate code that appears to be valid but may not actually be semantically or syntactically correct or may not accurately reflect the intent of the developer."
Interpretation limits: vendor statements of intended capability and risk, not measured net productivity, reliability, confidentiality guarantees, or proof of local suitability. Context processing makes permitted data exposure a decision question. Do not infer a specific retention, training-use, hosting or licensing term from these passages.
